name: 01_FOUNDATIONS.md
text:
# PERFUME 7 — Foundations
Version: 2026-10-07
Status: Working project source

## Core rule
**FEMININE ≠ SWEET ≠ SEXUAL.**

Perfume 7 rejects the automatic equation of femininity with sweetness, seduction, luxury, erotic availability, or desirability. Dark feminine fragrance need not mean rose, vanilla, amber, cherry, plum, sweet musk, or patchouli.

## Artistic direction
Translate myth, landscape, ritual, weather, intelligence, death, medicine, divinity, decay, and life into scent. Florals need not imply prettiness or sexual invitation. Darkness need not be edible or conventionally attractive.

## Critical principle
A perfume should not simply replace a soft feminine ideal with an equally observer-centered dark feminine ideal. Avoid describing every female figure as mysterious, irresistible, expensive, dangerous, or seductive.

## Working method
Separate historical evidence, mythological interpretation, olfactory metaphor, and actual tested formula. Preserve creative contradictions rather than flattening them into generic perfume marketing.

## Editorial conventions
Established decision = documented project direction. Concept = creative proposal, not tested formula. Historical claim = verify against primary or scholarly sources. Safety limits = verify with current material-specific documentation.

# PERFUME 7 — Fragrance Atlas
Version: 2026-10-07
Status: Concept inventory; not formulas

## Nyx
Cold air, night-blooming jasmine, ink, incense. Night as atmosphere, not seduction.

## Ereshkigal
Clay, mushroom, stone, extinguished smoke. Underworld, stillness, mineral weight.

## Izanami
Flowers decomposing into soil, mineral notes. Death and transformation rather than eroticized darkness.

## Iriomote Cat
Humid forest, hinoki, fungus, unseen animal. Concealment and habitat.

## Lilith / Bad Air
Dust, wind, bitter herbs, iron. A critical instrument for examining sexuality, external judgment, and self-policing; not a stock femme-fatale character.

## Joan of Arc
Rain, iron, wax, charcoal. Witness, ordeal, devotion, and material history.

## Mary Magdalene
Spikenard, salt, anointing resins, tomb stone. Anointing and mourning, not sexual reduction.

## Konohanasakuya-hime
Restrained sakura, charcoal, volcanic rock. Blossom and volcanic impermanence.

## Additional research candidates
Inari Ōkami; Tenjin; Izanagi; Japanese yōkai; Nefertem. These are research priorities, not finalized perfume formulas.

## Development fields for each entry
Narrative | Top/heart/base impression | Key materials | Accord sketch | Formula version | Safety review | Trial notes | Status.

name: 03_MATERIALS_ACCORDS.md
text:
# PERFUME 7 — Materials & Accords
Version: 2026-10-07
Status: Olfactory vocabulary, not a purchasing or safety list

## Material vocabulary recorded
Floral: night-blooming jasmine, sakura (restrained), lotus, orris, spikenard.
Wood/resin/smoke: hinoki, incense, anointing resins, charcoal, extinguished smoke.
Mineral/earth: clay, stone, volcanic rock, soil, iron impression, tomb stone impression.
Atmosphere: cold air, rain, wind, dust, humid forest, salt, seaweed.
Botanical/other: yuzu, tea, bitter herbs, camphor, mushroom/fungal impression, ink.

## Accord directions
- Cold nocturne: cold air + jasmine + ink + incense.
- Underworld mineral: clay + stone + fungus + spent smoke.
- Forest concealment: hinoki + humidity + soil/fungal atmosphere.
- Ritual aftermath: wax + charcoal + rain + metallic impression.
- Anointing/tomb: spikenard + resin + salt + stone.
- Volcanic blossom: restrained sakura + charcoal + rock.

## Important distinction
Some listed notes are impressions or accords, not literal materials appropriate for direct skin application. Metallic, fungal, smoke, stone, and atmospheric effects require appropriate perfumery construction and safety review.

## Record template
Material/accord | Odor description | Role | Source | Dilution | Compatibility | Restrictions | Trials | Notes.

name: 04_HISTORY_MYTHOLOGY.md
text:
# PERFUME 7 — History, Mythology & Ritual
Version: 2026-10-07
Status: Research framework; historical details require verification

## Four historical anchors
- Kyphi: ritual and transformation; investigate ancient Egyptian recipes and their variant traditions.
- Pomander: protection and contained atmosphere; investigate European material culture and changing recipes.
- Chypre: contrast and landscape; investigate Cyprus associations and François Coty's Chypre.
- Nefertem: divine association with fragrance itself; distinguish attested mythology from modern interpretation.

## Technical historical research
Tapputi; early extraction; heating, filtration, aromatic preparation, and the difference between historical descriptions and modern reconstructions.

## Japanese axis
Prioritize Konohanasakuya-hime, Inari Ōkami, Tenjin; extend to Izanagi, Izanami, and yōkai. Olfactory research palette: lotus, yuzu, hinoki, charcoal, tea, ink, soil, camphor, orris, seaweed, restrained sakura.

## Mythological interpretation rules
Avoid reducing Inanna, Ereshkigal, Lilith, Greek goddesses, or Egyptian goddesses to sexuality. Distinguish original texts, later reception, popular occult reinterpretation, and new creative readings. Veneration, archetypal use, and historical evidence are different categories.

## Citation fields
Claim | Tradition/text | Date/period | Translation/edition | Evidence | Interpretation | Confidence.

# PERFUME 7 — Formulation Lab
Version: 2026-10-07
Status: Laboratory structure; no verified quantitative formulas recovered

## Rule
Do not present an olfactory concept as a tested formula. Do not invent percentages, drops, concentrations, IFRA compliance, performance, or stability results.

## Experiment record template

Fragrance:

Goal:
Materials (supplier, exact identity, lot):

Skin test (only after safety assessment):
Projection/longevity observations:
Problems:
Revision:

## Current accord briefs to test
Nyx cold jasmine-ink-incense; Ereshkigal clay-fungus-stone-smoke; Izanami floral decomposition; Iriomote humid hinoki; Lilith dry bitter metallic air; Joan rain-wax-charcoal; Magdalene spikenard-resin-salt; Konohanasakuya-hime blossom-volcanic rock.

## Version control
Never overwrite previous trial observations. Assign sequential version identifiers and document every changed variable.

name: 06_SOURCING_SAFETY.md
text:
# PERFUME 7 — Sourcing, Equipment & Safety
Version: 2026-10-07
Status: Operational framework; supplier prices and limits not yet verified

## Procurement ledger
Material | Supplier | Product/chemical identity | CAS where applicable | Lot | Size | Price | Shipping | Unit cost | Date checked | SDS | IFRA certificate if applicable.

## Safety record
Record concentration, intended use category, dermal restrictions, sensitization concerns, phototoxicity, flammability, solvent handling, storage, labeling, and disposal. Verify against supplier SDS, relevant IFRA Standards, and applicable regulations.

## Permanent Bench Guide
Maintain a material-specific safety chart. Keep fragrance concentrate, dilution, and finished-product percentages distinct. Never infer safe skin use from a material's natural origin or traditional use.

## Equipment inventory
Track scale precision, vials, pipettes, blotters, protective equipment, labeling supplies, solvents, and storage. No particular equipment purchase has been confirmed in this source.

## Buying rules
Use verified current prices and shipping; distinguish desired materials from purchased inventory. No supplier, price, or quantitative formula is asserted here without a supporting record.

name: 07_RESEARCH_ARCHIVE.md
text:
# PERFUME 7 — Research Archive & Critical Theory
Version: 2026-10-07
Status: Research questions and critical framework

## Dark femininity thesis
Contemporary dark-feminine aesthetics often promise liberation from conventional femininity while preserving desirability as their organizing principle. The surface changes from innocent and soft to dangerous and irresistible; the imagined observer remains.

## Lilith / shadow work
The useful confrontation is not necessarily with a demon as an external entity, but with one's own relation to sexuality, self-surveillance, judgment, post-feminist contradiction, and self-policing.

Central question: **What remains when I stop watching myself being a woman?**

## Analytical lenses
Clothing; makeup; hair; body; sex; dating; luxury; speech; emotion; cronehood; appetite; interiors; fitness; photography; social media; witchcraft; tarot; astrology; horror; pornography; advertising; celebrity; mythology; death and decay.

Priority lenses: cronehood, appetite, anger, aging/death, labor.

## Discursive framework
Archetypes and symbolic classifications can function as discursive language for reflection and comparison without serving as diagnostic or ontological claims.

## Research agenda
Study scholarly literature and practitioner discussions, especially witchcraft forums, on dark femininity, feminist self-surveillance, sexuality, ritual symbolism, and commercialization. Keep firsthand claims separate from interpretation. Record full citations and quotations before making evidentiary claims.

## Archive entry template
Question | Source | Author/date | Primary/secondary/community | Evidence | Counterargument | Implications for Perfume 7 | Open questions.
